A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Dig-DEC research work. Their text, equations, tables, and figure support reliable comparison; both include complete Appendices A-J, which are unchanged.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical algorithms, regret bounds, and proofs. Tables 1-4 summarize analytical guarantees, and the three-armed bandit example is proved mathematically, without experimental results.

after.justification: v2 retains the theoretical results and appendices and adds explanatory passages. It reports no original experiments, simulations, user studies, or empirical data analyses.

M1.justification: The Dig-DEC objective, minimax decision rule, batching estimator, and two-level posterior update remain unchanged in Algorithms 1-4. The added explanations do not revise these procedures.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or empirical evaluation tasks. The new linear-MDP example in Section 3.2 illustrates assumptions; it does not introduce an evaluated scenario.

E2.justification: Neither version empirically evaluates comparison methods. The theoretical comparator sets in Tables 3-4, including Foster et al. (2023b) and Liu et al. (2025), are unchanged.

E3.justification: No experimental evaluation protocols are reported in either version. The new on-policy/off-policy explanation describes existing theoretical subclasses, without changing settings or procedures.

E4.justification: No ablations, robustness tests, or empirical supplementary analyses are added or removed. The analytical three-armed bandit example in Theorem 14 and Appendix J is unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The concentration inequalities and probabilistic guarantees in the theoretical analysis are unchanged.

E6.justification: All regret bounds and comparisons in Tables 1-4 are retained. Theorem 14 still contrasts regret at most 1 for the proposed algorithm with an Omega(sqrt(T)) lower bound for Foster et al. (2023b); no empirical results are added.

T1.justification: The new Section 3.2 example asserts equivalence between equality of Q-functions at every state-action pair and equality of expected per-step feature vectors. This adds a converse beyond the unchanged one-way statement in Lemma 37. The numbered assumptions, theorems, and appendix proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction now explicitly qualify the hybrid-MDP guarantee with linear rewards. This narrows the headline wording to reflect the restriction already present in v1's Assumption 4 and Table 4; the principal contributions and regret guarantees are retained.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 newly interprets Assumptions 5-6 through realizability and Bellman completeness. Section 5.1 explains the on-policy/off-policy terminology and attributes the regret difference to whether an additional exploration policy is needed. Existing limitations concerning unknown reward features remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Algorithm pseudocode and parameter choices, including the estimation procedures in Appendices F-G, are unchanged. No implementation, hardware, code, or data-access information is added.

R1.justification: The bibliography is unchanged, but v2 adds specific connections to Liu et al. (2024b)'s linear MDPs, Du et al. (2021)'s estimation-error terminology, and Jin et al. (2021)'s Q-type/V-type distinction. These modestly expand the contextualization of the existing framework.

P1.justification: Four localized explanatory passages are added in Sections 3.2, 4.2, and 5.1, alongside short wording edits and removal of the unused 'decouplable MDPs' label. The section organization and appendix text remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 2 moves from page 10 to page 11, equation spacing and page breaks shift, and Table 1's caption receives a small wording edit. Table structures, Figure 1, and appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 improves scope accuracy by explicitly stating the linear-reward restriction and adds useful explanations. However, its new Section 3.2 equivalence introduces a mathematical concern: matching feature expectations along a policy need not determine Q-values for unchosen actions, and unchanged Lemma 37 establishes only one direction. The main results and proofs are unchanged. These clarity gains and the new reliability concern leave the net quality change uncertain.
